summary: Spanish-built 1898 light on Punta Morrillos at Arecibo: its keepers from 1901 to 1964, the wind-driven plant, the 1970s vandalism and the park.

structures.note: about 15 m including lantern and cupola (NRHP); the archive gives 40 ft from base to lantern
two units for a first-class and a third-class keeper (NRHP); LighthouseFriends describes identical five-room apartments

access.note: The archive lists the light as open to the public. The park is on the site with paid entry; the lighthouse is a museum.

visit.note: Arecibo Lighthouse & Historical Park; hours and admission fees on the park's website

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (owner, per LighthouseFriends and the 1977 nomination); the park is run as a nonprofit

events.note: Station established 1898 (archive); first lens installed 1898 per archive, 1897 per NRHP
Third-order Fresnel lens made in Paris (1897 per NRHP; 1898 per archive)
Wind-driven electric plant installed, September 1926 per the 1928 Bulletin (the 1938 Bulletin says 1930)
Wind electric plant installed in 1930 (1938 Bulletin)
Incandescent oil-vapor system replaced by an electric lamp hooked to a windmill
Keepers' quarters remodeled with bathrooms; brick roof replaced with reinforced concrete
Vandalized 16 times between 29 Oct 1969 and 28 Oct 1977
Almost all of the lantern and the entire lens destroyed
City of Arecibo began an ambitious restoration; a new lantern was installed by 2002

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1928 Bulletin dates the wind-driven plant to September 1926; the 1938 Bulletin dates the installation to 1930. The story gives both and does not choose.
The 1977 nomination says the tower and dwelling were painted white with lead-gray trim; LighthouseFriends says red with lead-gray trim.
The NRHP nomination dates the 3rd-order lens to 1897; the USLHS archive gives 1898 as the year the original lens was installed. The story gives both and does not choose.

corrections.proposed: hexagonal tower attached to the north face of a rectangular dwelling
corrections.why: The NRHP nomination describes an hexagonal tower attached to the north facade of a rectangular dwelling; the USLHS record gives 'HEXAGONAL ATT. TO RECTANGUALAR BLDG'. 'Conical' is not supported by either source.

notes_for_editor: 1) NRHP nomination: the text is OCR and some words are garbled; quotes were checked against the OCR. The lens maker is printed as 'Earbier & Bernard' in the OCR (LighthouseFriends gives Barbier & Benard); the story avoids naming the maker. 2) The 1900 Light-House Board construction table (printed p.69, OCR, column-aligned) names Arecibo, and the index gives 'Arecibo, P. R 69'. The table's begun dates appear to give 1896 for Arecibo, but column alignment is unreliable in the OCR, so no date from that table is used. Check the page image before using any of its dates. 3) The Board's 1900 report gives two dates for the transfer of the Porto Rican service (1 May 1899 and 1 May 1900); the story does not use either. 4) Current status: the archive says active with optic '190 MM'; LighthouseFriends says the station was disestablished in 1964; the record's Fl W 5s characteristic is not checked against a current source. 5) Chronicling America searches for Arecibo in Puerto Rico papers returned no readable result (one timed out; the background run produced no output); no newspaper evidence is used. 6) The Coast Guard Historian's page on the light (archived copy) returned HTTP 403; HAER PR-38 on loc.gov was not read (loc.gov is not called directly). 7) No woman keeper appears in the sources read. 8) Keepers after about 1960 are named only as the archive roster prints them. 9) No wreck or rescue tied to the light was found in the sources read. 10) Wikipedia (English and Spanish) was used for leads only. 11) Tower height: NRHP gives about 15 m including the lantern and cupola; the record gives 14 m. 12) Lens date: NRHP says 1897 (Earbier & Bernard lens); the archive says 1898 (year original lens installed). Both given in the story. 13) The station record's light characteristic (Fl W 5s) was not checked against a current source; NRHP records a characteristic change in 1930 (Fl. 20s) and again in 1977 without naming the new one. 14) The park's website is in Spanish. The story paraphrases it; the evidence quotes are in Spanish with the English gloss in the story. 15) Fact-check 2026-10-22: the earlier draft said the 1900 Porto Rico section did not name Arecibo. That was wrong: the section's construction table on printed p.69 lists Arecibo. The story now says so and takes no date from the table. 16) The 1928 Bulletin (PDF p.19) and the 1938 Bulletin (PDF p.7) were checked on the PDF text; the wind-plant dates (September 1926 and 1930) conflict and the story states both. 17) The Index 1912-1917 entry for Castillo's efficiency pennant gives Bulletin page 47; the story cites the index as the source for that entry.
